'''Geji''' (Gezawa) is a minor [[Chadic languages|Chadic]] [[dialect cluster]] of [[Bauchi State]], Nigeria. The three varieties are Buu, Gyaazi and Mәgang (Mugan). The latter two are quite similar.<ref name="Blench">Blench, Roger. 2020. ''[https://www.academia.edu/44809765/An_introduction_to_Mәgang_a_South_Bauchi_language_of_Central_Nigeria An introduction to Mәgang, a South Bauchi language of Central Nigeria]''.</ref>

==Varieties==

Blench (2020) lists:<ref name="Blench"/>

*Buu
*Gyaazi, Mәgang

Zaranda, an exonym for Bu, endonym ''Bùù'', is a Chadic language spoken in the South of Bauchi State, in Nigeria, belonging to the South-Bauchi West group of Chadic languages (Shimizu 1978). Although generally associated with Bolu, Pelu and Geji, Buu stands apart from these other lects with which there is no intercomprehension. Most of the Buu population has migrated from the original location of the 
Zaranda village (Zaranda Habe, longitude 9,57; latitude 10,28) to the present Zaranda (longitude 9,52; latitude 10,23) where they have abandoned their language for Hausa and Fulfulde. The few that have retained their language live in Zaranda Habe, in houses scattered in the hills, gathering around the chief once a year for the traditional religious festivities. It is believed to be clearly distinct and probably a separate language.<ref>[https://www.academia.edu/1284711/Bu_aka_Zaranda_Chadic_South_Bauchi_West_Wordlist_and_grammatical_notes Buu-Zaranda]</ref>

Gezawa, Gaejawa are exonyms for Geji, endonym ''Gyaazә''. Bagba is a loconym.
